svg.aria-label: How to write ಢ: 3 strokes · 2 pen lifts · 7 movements
svg.title: Writing ಢ
svg.desc: 7 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ಢ (kannada), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansKannada-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-dda.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಢ, 52 frames, 5.2 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016) <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kannada-alphabet-dda.gif>. Source note on variation: The CC BY-SA 4.0 animation is filed under the slug "dda" and draws retroflex ಢ (U+0CA2); in this series "da" animates ಡ and dental ದ is "dha", so the glyph was checked frame by frame rather than taken from the file name. It writes ಢ in three pen-down runs: from the upper left the pen goes down around the left lobe, up into the middle point, down around the right lobe and up the right side, curls left into the small inner loop and round it, then rises out of it and arcs back left across the top (frames 0–29); after a lift, the top bar from left to right curling up into the hook (frames 30–35); after a second lift, the tail below the point, drawn downward (frames 39–40). Its body is ಡ's. The frames were read from a mirror copy that matches the Commons file's listed size (244×173, 165 KB) and byte size. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Kannada outline rather than copying the animation's handwritten proportions; in that outline the arc across the top is fused into the bar and the loop's right side is shared with the rise to the bar, so the closing movement runs along the lower part of the bar's ink, the bar retraces it and the shared stretch is drawn twice, and the tail is a short tapered bar. The two-lift order remains the same.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 strokes · 2 pen lifts · 7 movements
Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-dda.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಢ, 52 frames, 5.2 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
